extra.message: User-supplied 'host' GET parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary commands via the 'host' parameter (e.g., '127.0.0.1; rm -rf /').
Untrusted data from request body or GET parameter 'blob' is deserialized with pickle.loads(). Pickle deserialization can execute arbitrary Python code, leading to total server compromise.

User-controlled 'fragment' GET parameter is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), which can lead to remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escapes.

XML parser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False on user-supplied XML from request.body. This enables XXE (XML External Entity) attacks, allowing file disclosure, SSRF, and denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User-controlled JSON payload from request body is passed directly as a MongoDB query filter. An attacker can inject arbitrary MongoDB query operators (e.g., $gt, $regex, $where) to bypass authentication, extract data, or perform other unauthorized operations.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: User-controlled 'ref' GET parameter is used to construct a file path (f"{ref}.json") and then written to disk via target.write_text(). An attacker can use path traversal sequences like '../../etc/crontab' to write arbitrary files anywhere on the filesystem, potentially gaining code execution.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User-controlled filename from uploaded file (drop_blob.name) or GET parameter 'packet_ref' is passed to FileSystemStorage.save() without sanitization. An attacker can provide filenames containing '../' sequences to write files outside the intended directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User-controlled GET/POST parameter 'lane' is passed directly to Django's redirect() function. An attacker can use this to redirect users to arbitrary external websites (e.g., phishing pages) by providing a fully qualified URL like 'https://evil.com'.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Django SECRET_KEY has a hardcoded fallback value 'django-insecure-local-dev-only'. If the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set, this weak, well-known key is used. This allows session forging, CSRF token prediction, and other cryptographic bypass attacks.

Default database connection credentials (user: lms_user, password: lms_pass) are hardcoded in settings.py. If the DATABASE_URL environment variable is not set, these weak, well-known credentials are used to connect to the PostgreSQL database.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is set to the value of the Origin request header (reflected) with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials set to 'true'. This allows any external site to make authenticated cross-origin requests, enabling credential theft via CORS-based attacks.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Sensitive personally identifiable information (SSN and credit card numbers) is accepted via GET parameters ('ssn' and 'card') and written to a JSON file on the server's filesystem. GET parameters are logged in server access logs, bookmarked, and cached by browsers, making this a severe data leak vector.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: SSL certificate verification is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context() when making an HTTPS request to an external endpoint. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks to intercept or modify the traffic.

Response headers explicitly set X-XSS-Protection to '0' (disabling browser XSS filters) and Content-Security-Policy to an empty string (disabling CSP). This weakens browser-side security protections, making XSS attacks significantly easier to exploit.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

extra.message: assignment_status view performs a state-changing operation (changes assignment status in the database) but accepts GET requests without CSRF protection. Django's CSRF middleware only protects POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH. An attacker can forge a request via an tag or link to change assignment status on behalf of an authenticated instructor.

release_grade view performs a state-changing operation (releases grades to students) but accepts GET requests without CSRF protection. Django's CSRF middleware only protects POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH. An attacker can forge a request to release grades on behalf of an authenticated instructor.

request_resubmission view performs a state-changing operation (changes submission status to 'needs_resubmission') but accepts GET requests without CSRF protection. An attacker can forge a request to force resubmission on behalf of an authenticated instructor.

admin_user_toggle view performs a state-changing operation (disables/enables user accounts) but accepts GET requests without CSRF protection. An attacker can forge a request to disable any user account on behalf of an authenticated school admin.

discussion_moderate view performs a state-changing operation (changes thread status to pinned/locked/hidden/open) but accepts GET requests without CSRF protection. An attacker can forge a request to moderate discussion threads on behalf of an authenticated instructor.
